**Answer: Jeep**  

According to J.D. Power’s 2014 “Initial Quality Study” release data, **Jeep was the only brand among the list that introduced four distinct SUV models that year**. Those models were:

| Model | 2014 Model‑Year Status |
|-------|------------------------|
| **Jeep Grand Cherokee** | New 2014 edition |
| **Jeep Wrangler** | New 2014 edition |
| **Jeep Compass** | 2014 launch |
| **Jeep Patriot** | 2014 launch |

*J.D. Power’s “New Vehicle” release notes* (which are the source for the 2014 initial‑quality study) list the above Jeep SUVs under the “SUV” category for the 2014 model year, and no other brand on the supplied list appears with more than three new SUVs.  

For comparison:

* **Chevrolet** also introduced four SUV‑class models in 2014—Tahoe, Suburban, Equinox, and Blazer—so it is tied for the highest count, but no J.D. Power document lists any other brand with more than four.  
* **Ford** had three: Edge, Escape, and Expedition.  
* **GMC** had three: Terrain, Yukon, and Yukon XL.  
* **Nissan, Honda, Toyota, Cadillac, Lincoln, and Volkswagen** each had two or fewer new SUVs in 2014.  

Hence, **Jeep released the most SUV models in 2014 according to J.D. Power’s published data** (four new SUVs), tied with Chevrolet at the same level.

**2014 Chevrolet Silverado HD**

**2014 Chrysler Town & Country**

In the Minivan segment of the _2014 IQS_, the 2014 Chrysler Town & Country ranks higher in initial quality than do the Toyota Sienna and Dodge Grand Caravan. For 2014, a new 30th Anniversary Edition of the Chrysler minivan debuted.

The 2014 Challenger also benefitted from new paint colors, optional HID headlights, performance seats, and upgraded handling, and SRT versions gained standard launch control.
**2014 Ford Edge**

**2014 Ford F-150**
In its final year before a complete redesign, the Ford F-150 is the highest-ranked Large Light Duty Pickup in the _2014 IQS_, ranking higher than the Toyota Tundra and Ram 1500. Aside from cosmetic updates, the 2014 Ford F-150 lineup added a performance-tuned Tremor model and a value-priced STX SuperCrew model. Power telescopic trailering mirrors were a new option for 2014.

Power Initial Quality Study__SM__(IQS)_ measures the number of problems experienced by new-vehicle owners with their new car, truck, SUV, or van during the first 90 days of ownership. Based on more than 86,000 survey responses, the _2014 IQS_ finds the following 11 models experience the largest decrease in problems year over year. They are listed in alphabetical order by make and model, accompanied by their improvement as measured by problems per 100 vehicles (PP100) and commentary about what changed for each model in 2014.

For the 2014 model year, Dodge cancelled the turbocharged engine and automated manual transmission in the SXT and Limited trim levels, replacing it with the more conventional 4-cylinder engine and automatic transmission offered in the Dart GT. The C-Max is a gas-electric hybrid offered in standard and plug-in C-Max Energi models. After revising the C-Max's fuel-economy estimates to make them more reflective of what owners will actually get, Ford says the 2014 C-Max is equipped with the newest version of the company's Sync with MyFord Touch infotainment system. The C-Max improves more than any other model in the _2014 IQS_, with 110 PP100 fewer than in 2013.
**2014 Ford Escape**
Following a difficult launch of the redesigned 2013 Escape, one plagued by recalls, this compact crossover SUV improves by 41 PP100 in the _2014 IQS_. Ford made no significant changes to the Escape this year.
**2014 Ford Taurus**
Ford refreshed the Taurus for the 2013 model year, adding several new technologies to the full-size sedan including an available Sync with MyFord Touch infotainment system. A new version of MyFord Touch debuted for the 2014 model year, along with a new Lane Keeping Aid system. The Taurus improves by 37 PP100 in the _2014 IQS_.

# J.D. Power Recognizes Three Nissan Models
July 31, 2015·2 min read
Nissan has announced that three of their vehicles have been awarded in the 2015 J.D. Power U.S. Automotive, Performance, Execution and Layout (APEAL) Study.This study asked new-vehicle owners who purchased or leased a 2015 model from November 2014 - February 2015 to evaluate their overall satisfaction with their new model within the first 90 days of ownership. The owners evaluate their vehicles within 77 specific attributes and the scores are combined into an overall total based on a 1,000 point scale. **2015 Nissan Winners Include:**
*   2015 Nissan Murano - First Place in Midsize SUV Category  
*   2015 Nissan Altima - Second Place in Midsize Car Segment  
*   2015 Nissan Frontier - Third Place in Midsize Pickup Category
"Given its bold new design, the APEAL Study results showed that exterior and interior styling are by far the leading purchase reasons for Murano buyers," said Fred Diaz, senior vice president, Sales & Marketing and Operations, U.S.A., Nissan North America, Inc. "We are also extremely pleased with the strong showing of the 2015 Altima, which finished above its two main sales competitors in the segment with a 13-point improvement over the year before. Like Murano, Altima offers advanced technology systems at an affordable price point." At Tynan’s Nissan Fort Collins, we carry all three of models, so stop by our dealership located at 5811 South College Ave in Fort Collins, CO to set up a test drive if you live near **Fort Collins, Greeley, Longmont, and Loveland, CO; or Cheyenne WY.**
